stem: An adult client's oral temperature is 39.2°C (102.6°F). How should the nurse interpret this finding?

options.A: Interpret the value as within the expected adult oral range and continue routine observation unless other vital signs become abnormal.
options.B: Interpret the value as hypothermia and begin warming measures before evaluating symptoms or possible causes.
options.C: Treat the value as a minor variation from normal and defer illness assessment unless a later measurement rises further.
options.D: Recognize the value as fever and assess the client's symptoms and clinical context for a possible underlying cause.

rationale: MedlinePlus states that a high body temperature is fever, gives an average normal oral temperature of 37°C (98.6°F), and states that a reading more than about 1–1.5°F above a person's normal temperature is fever. It also lists infection and multiple noninfectious causes. An oral temperature of 39.2°C (102.6°F) is therefore clearly febrile. D is correct; A and C underclassify the finding, and B reverses it.
educational_objective: Recognize a markedly elevated adult oral temperature as fever and assess associated symptoms and clinical context rather than misclassifying or dismissing the finding.
source_version_date: Review Date January 14, 2026; live page retrieved 2026-08-26
source_locator: Normal Results: average normal oral temperature 98.6°F (37°C); What Abnormal Results Mean: >1–1.5°F above normal is fever; fever may reflect infection or other medical problems.
source_claim_supported: An adult oral temperature of 39.2°C is clearly febrile and should be interpreted in clinical context.
blueprint_locator: Reduction of Risk Potential — focused assessment, recognition of abnormal findings, and monitoring changes in condition.
correction_summary: Removed distractor-only absolute wording and rebuilt all options as parallel temperature interpretations.

audit_findings.independent_adversarial_second_pass: PASS — 39.2°C is far above the cited oral normal/fever range; no alternate option is defensible.
